body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 16, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high near 98° and air quality at a moderate 64. Overnight, a tragic wrong-way crash on Highway 99 claimed three lives, and we’ll have the details on that and more. For now, pour some coffee and let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a wrong-way driver collided with two other vehicles around 12:44 a.m. The crash left three people dead and drew a heavy emergency response, including Metro 3, medic squad 63, and Truck 65 as the rescue group. Crews worked to extricate two patients from the wreckage, both of whom were able to walk (green tag). Meanwhile, in southeast Bakersfield, a palm tree fire spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way around 9:16 p.m., prompting a reinforced alarm with Engine 7 taking incident command. Around the county, officers staged on a possible shooting on Price Street that never developed on the air, chased a DUI driver in a white BMW east from the 33rd Street area, and responded to a long string of low-stakes domestics and disturbances — including a Camellia Village apartment where a wall was punched in.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 86° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 64.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early Sunday morning.** According to California Highway Patrol Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire, and all three occupants inside that vehicle died from their injuries. The driver and one other occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the two occupants in the Chevrolet sustained minor injuries. Authorities say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield police and fire chiefs shared Fourth of July findings at a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city.** Bakersfield Fire Chief Kevin Albertson noted that the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with significant injuries and even deaths from fireworks. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. City Councilman Eric Arias mentioned that stronger policies are in the works to deter illegal fireworks use.

**23ABC shares that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, recently traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up.** Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Urban Development, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development. Baldovinos said one of the most debated topics during the two-day Washington meeting was how long recovery should last, and he pushed back on the view that recovery should only be for a treatment program of 28 days, drawing on his own experience to emphasize that recovery is a long-term process.

## Something good

Kern County’s own Carlos Baldovinos is making a national impact by helping shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community. This effort, developed with input from professionals across the country, provides resources and support for those struggling with addiction, potentially improving the lives of many individuals in our community and beyond.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar for this week. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. And on Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. Meanwhile, the Fox Theater has a busy lineup of shows, including Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22; Rodney Carrington on August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28; Willie Barcena on August 29; and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix, also on August 29. Finally, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA takes the stage on September 4.
